claims.evidence: Diabetes UK: no single diabetes diet, healthier choices more often; NICE 1.3.3 emphasise healthy balanced eating applicable to the general population.
Diabetes UK: no single diabetes diet; healthier choices more often.
Diabetes UK: total amount of carbohydrate eaten has the biggest effect on glucose levels after eating.
NICE 1.3.5: for adults with type 2 diabetes who are overweight, set an initial body weight loss target of 5-10%.
NICE 1.3.1: individualised and ongoing nutritional advice from a healthcare professional with specific expertise and competencies in nutrition.
Diabetes UK: no single diabetes diet; list of forbidden foods outdated.
Diabetes UK: make healthier choices more often and keep treats occasional and small.
NICE 1.3.3: emphasise advice on healthy balanced eating applicable to the general population.
NHS food page: physical exercise helps lower blood sugar; short-term low-calorie diets linked to lower blood sugar; limit certain foods.
Diabetes UK advises avoiding foods labelled 'diabetic' or 'suitable for diabetics'; the 'against the law' claim and 'high in fat, expensive' not found in retrieved text.
claims.newSentence: Diabetes UK advises avoiding foods labelled 'diabetic' or 'suitable for diabetics'.

claims.evidence: NICE: discourage adults with type 2 diabetes from using foods marketed specifically for people with diabetes.
'Everyone needs carbohydrate' not seen verbatim; Diabetes UK says low-carb eating shouldn't be no-carb eating.
claims.newSentence: Diabetes UK says that even low-carb eating shouldn't be no-carb eating.

claims.evidence: Same as c03.
Diabetes UK: choosing high-fibre wholegrain foods instead of refined carbs such as white bread is better for heart health; white rice not mentioned in retrieved text.
claims.newSentence: Its guidance favours higher-fibre wholegrain foods over refined carbohydrates such as white bread.

claims.evidence: NICE individualised-advice recommendation found, but 'carbohydrate, alcohol and meal patterns' wording not found; duplicates c27.
NICE: can substitute a limited amount of sucrose-containing foods for other carbohydrates in the meal plan but take care to avoid excess energy intake.
Diabetes UK: whole fruit is good for everyone, including people with diabetes.
Diabetes UK type 2 meal plan contains at least five portions of fruit and veg a day; 'watch fruit portion sizes because of carbohydrate' not found.
claims.newSentence: Diabetes UK's type 2 meal plan includes at least five portions of fruit and vegetables a day.

claims.evidence: Diabetes UK lists kidney beans, chickpeas and lentils as protein sources and suggests beans and pulses to replace some or all of the meat; eggs also discussed; 'meat not needed every day' and nuts not confirmed.
claims.newSentence: Diabetes UK lists pulses such as kidney beans, chickpeas and lentils as protein sources, and suggests using beans and pulses to replace some or all of the meat in a dish.

claims.evidence: Diabetes UK recommends at least two portions of oily fish each week, not 'one or two'.
claims.newSentence: It recommends at least two portions of oily fish each week.

claims.evidence: North Bristol NHS Trust page: half vegetables or salad, quarter starchy carbohydrate, quarter meat, fish, cheese, eggs or pulses (in its weight-loss section; elsewhere it uses a larger starch share).
claims.newSentence: One NHS trust leaflet (North Bristol) describes, in its weight-loss section, a plate with half vegetables or salad, a quarter starchy carbohydrate foods, and a quarter meat, fish, cheese, eggs or pulses.

claims.evidence: NICE 1.3.5: initial body weight loss target 5-10% for overweight adults.
NICE: lesser weight loss may still be of benefit; larger losses in the longer term have advantageous metabolic impact.
NHS treatment page text not retrieved (title only); claim not verified. Food page does say exercise lowers blood sugar (covered by c09).
NHS food page: aim for at least 2.5 hours of activity a week; examples brisk walking, climbing stairs, more vigorous housework or gardening. Source says 'at least', not 'about'.
claims.newSentence: The NHS page on food and keeping active suggests at least two and a half hours of activity a week, with brisk walking, climbing stairs and more vigorous housework or gardening as examples.

claims.evidence: NHS: short-term low-calorie diets (800-1,200 calories a day for about 12 weeks) linked to weight loss and lower blood sugar; not safe or suitable for everyone. 'Medical advice first' wording not verified verbatim.
claims.newSentence: The same page describes a short-term low-calorie diet as linked to weight loss and lower blood sugar in some people, and says it is not safe or suitable for everyone with type 2 diabetes.

claims.evidence: NICE 1.3.1 and 1.3.2: individualised, ongoing advice from a professional with nutrition expertise, sensitive to needs, culture and beliefs.
Not found in NICE text retrieved. NHS food page says avoid missing meals if taking medicines that can cause hypos.
claims.newSentence: The NHS notes that people taking medicines that can cause hypos are advised not to miss meals.
